passages.text: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks these words.
The Teacher is the son of David.
The Teacher is king in Jerusalem.
The Teacher says, “Futility of futilities.”
The Teacher says, “Everything is futile.”
passages.original: דִּבְרֵי֙ קֹהֶ֣לֶת בֶּן־ דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ הֲבֵ֤ל הֲבָלִים֙ אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת הֲבֵ֥ל הֲבָלִ֖ים הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?
passages.sermon:
The Teacher is the son of David.
He is the king in Jerusalem.
He asks a question about people.
He asks, “What does a person gain?”
He means, “What profit does a person have?”
He is talking about all the work a person does.
He says a person works hard under the sun.
He asks if there is any real benefit from all this effort.
passages.original: מַה־ יִּתְר֖וֹן לָֽאָדָ֑ם בְּכָל־ עֲמָל֔וֹ שֶֽׁיַּעֲמֹ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks.
The Teacher is the son of David.
The Teacher is king in Jerusalem.
People are born.
People die.
Generations arrive.
Generations depart.
The earth stays the same.
The earth remains forever.
passages.original: דּ֤וֹר הֹלֵךְ֙ וְד֣וֹר בָּ֔א וְהָאָ֖רֶץ לְעוֹלָ֥ם עֹמָֽדֶת׃

passages.text: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.
passages.sermon: The sun rises.\r\nThe sun sets.\r\nThe sun quickly returns to the place where it rises.
passages.original: וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל־ מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.
passages.sermon:
The wind moves.
The wind goes toward the south.
The wind turns toward the north.
The wind keeps circling around and around.
The wind always returns to its path.
The wind never stops its cycle.
passages.original: הוֹלֵךְ֙ אֶל־ דָּר֔וֹם וְסוֹבֵ֖ב אֶל־ צָפ֑וֹן סוֹבֵ֤ב׀ סֹבֵב֙ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָר֔וּחַ וְעַל־ סְבִיבֹתָ֖יו שָׁ֥ב הָרֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.
passages.sermon:
All rivers flow into the sea.
The sea is never full.
Rivers return to the place they came from.
Rivers flow again to the sea.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹלְכִ֣ים אֶל־ הַיָּ֔ם וְהַיָּ֖ם אֵינֶ֣נּוּ מָלֵ֑א אֶל־ מְק֗וֹם שֶׁ֤הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹֽלְכִ֔ים שָׁ֛ם הֵ֥ם שָׁבִ֖ים לָלָֽכֶת׃

passages.text: All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.
passages.sermon:
Everything in life brings weariness.
No one can fully explain it.
The human eye always wants to see more.
The human ear never has enough of hearing.
passages.original: כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים יְגֵעִ֔ים לֹא־ יוּכַ֥ל אִ֖ישׁ לְדַבֵּ֑ר לֹא־ תִשְׂבַּ֥ע עַ֙יִן֙ לִרְא֔וֹת וְלֹא־ תִמָּלֵ֥א אֹ֖זֶן מִשְּׁמֹֽעַ׃

passages.text: What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
The Teacher speaks about life.
What has happened before will happen again.
What people have done before will be done again.
Nothing is truly new under the sun.
passages.original: מַה־ שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ ה֣וּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֔ה וּמַה־ שֶׁנַּֽעֲשָׂ֔ה ה֖וּא שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין כָּל־ חָדָ֖שׁ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks.
The Teacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
People may say, “Look, this is new.”
This thing is not truly new.
It has already existed long ago.
It existed in the ages before us.
passages.original: יֵ֥שׁ דָּבָ֛ר שֶׁיֹּאמַ֥ר רְאֵה־ זֶ֖ה חָדָ֣שׁ ה֑וּא כְּבָר֙ הָיָ֣ה לְעֹֽלָמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה מִלְּפָנֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.
passages.sermon:
People forget those who lived before us.
Future generations will also be forgotten.
Those who come later will not remember those who came before them.
No one will remember the people who come after, either.
Remembrance does not last from one generation to the next.
passages.original: אֵ֥ין זִכְר֖וֹן לָרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וְגַ֨ם לָאַחֲרֹנִ֜ים שֶׁיִּהְי֗וּ לֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ זִכָּר֔וֹן עִ֥ם שֶׁיִּהְי֖וּ לָאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃פ

passages.text: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: I am the Teacher.\r\nI was king over Israel.\r\nI ruled in Jerusalem.
passages.original: אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a heavy burden God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!
passages.sermon:
I am the Teacher.
I was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I set my mind to seek wisdom.
I explored everything done under heaven.
God has given people a hard task.
This task keeps them busy.
This burden is heavy.
passages.original: וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת־ לִבִּ֗י לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙ בַּֽחָכְמָ֔ה עַ֛ל כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם ה֣וּא׀ עִנְיַ֣ן רָ֗ע נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.
passages.sermon:
I am the Teacher.
I was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
I have seen all the things people do under the sun.
Everything people do is meaningless.
All these actions are like chasing the wind.
passages.original: רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֔ים שֶֽׁנַּעֲשׂ֖וּ תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
passages.sermon:
Some things are crooked.
No one can make them straight.
Some things are missing.
No one can count what is not there.
passages.original: מְעֻוָּ֖ת לֹא־ יוּכַ֣ל לִתְקֹ֑ן וְחֶסְר֖וֹן לֹא־ יוּכַ֥ל לְהִמָּנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.  
King Solomon ruled over Jerusalem.  
King Solomon spoke to himself.  
He said, "I have grown in wisdom."  
He said, "I have increased in wisdom more than anyone before me in Jerusalem."  
His mind saw much wisdom.  
His mind saw much knowledge.
passages.original: דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם־ לִבִּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲנִ֗י הִנֵּ֨ה הִגְדַּ֤לְתִּי וְהוֹסַ֙פְתִּי֙ חָכְמָ֔ה עַ֛ל כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ הָיָ֥ה לְפָנַ֖י עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלִבִּ֛י רָאָ֥ה הַרְבֵּ֖ה חָכְמָ֥ה וָדָֽעַת׃

passages.text: So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is King Solomon.
King Solomon ruled over Jerusalem.
King Solomon was known for his great wisdom.
King Solomon decided to understand wisdom.
He also decided to understand madness.
He also decided to understand foolishness.
King Solomon learned something important.
He learned that seeking all these things is pointless.
He saw that chasing wisdom, madness, and foolishness is like chasing the wind.
passages.original: וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֔ה וְדַ֥עַת הוֹלֵל֖וֹת וְשִׂכְל֑וּת יָדַ֕עְתִּי שֶׁגַּם־ זֶ֥ה ה֖וּא רַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king in Jerusalem.
Solomon had great wisdom.
Solomon learned an important truth.
When a person gains much wisdom, that person also finds much sorrow.
When a person increases knowledge, that person also increases grief.
passages.original: כִּ֛י בְּרֹ֥ב חָכְמָ֖ה רָב־ כָּ֑עַס וְיוֹסִ֥יף דַּ֖עַת יוֹסִ֥יף מַכְאֽוֹב׃
